pr_title: Fetch formula resources before unlinking during upgrade.
pr_body:
- [x] Have you followed the guidelines in our [Contributing](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) document?
- [x] Have you checked to ensure there aren't other open [Pull Requests](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pulls) for the same change?
- [x] Have you added an explanation of what your changes do and why you'd like us to include them?
- [ ] Have you written new tests for your changes? [Here's an example](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/Library/Homebrew/test/PATH_spec.rb).
- [x] Have you successfully run `brew style` with your changes locally?
- [ ] Have you successfully run `brew tests` with your changes locally?

-----

This updates the `brew upgrade` command. Upgrading default behavior will now fetch remote resources before unlinking, and then install the new version as requested in #6339 

Fixes #6374.
pr_comments:
I added an optional flag `--download-silently` when using the `install` command and when `build` is called inside of `formula_installer` which would silence the downloading  `ohai` when passed in. This takes care of duplication when it comes to non-bottles without needing to pass in any arguments to `download_strategy`. 

Upon testing, I did find duplication for bottles too, which @MikeMcQuaid  pointed out above and initially I had misunderstood. Though, that was solved with just checking if the `formula_installer` had already fetched.

@MikeMcQuaid 

If I could possibly have some clarification or preference as to the preferred way to tackle this. 

Option 1:
Pass in an argument to `downloader.fetch` that gets called inside of `fetch` in `formula_installer`.

So, the first time `downloader.fetch` is called, we will not print out the 'downloading' message, however the behavior remains the same. 

Instead, we will print it out when `build` gets called in another process(which happens during `install`), and keep in mind that when `build` is called, it is being fetched again.

The trade off here is, we will get the 'already downloaded' message as shown in the example below:

```
==> Downloading https://curl.haxx.se/download/curl-7.69.1.tar.bz2

```

Instead of the downloading message below:

```
==> Downloading https://curl.haxx.se/download/curl-7.69.1.tar.bz2
######################################################################## 100.0%
```

Option 2:

Keep things as is and move `ARGV` to `Homebrew.args`.

@MichelleNguy I think there's an Option 3 where we pass through a parameter to `build.rb` that we've already attempted to fetch (or vice-versa and pass a parameter every time not called from `build.rb`) . It might be a few days before I can take a look at that, though.

I've had a look. An issue I noticed with this PR as-is is that it won't handle the fetch of dependencies that are needed. It'd be desirable to do this, I think. Check out `FormulaInstaller#install_dependency` and `FormulaInstaller#install_dependencies`; I think you'd want something similar like `FormulaInstaller#fetch_dependency` and `FormulaInstaller#fetch_dependencies` which are called by `FormulaInstaller#fetch` and call ``FormulaInstaller#fetch` on all dependencies. You may wish to use/share code with `cmd/fetch.rb` which can currently be used for fetching formulae and their resources.

My suggestion for moving forward would be to separate the `fetch` and `build` (`pour` or `stage`  as appropriate when building from bottle or from source). `pour` should not fetch the bottle at all and `Resource#stage` should not fetch either; both should operate with the assumption that the fetch has already been done by an earlier stage.

1. Regarding https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/7124#issuecomment-618984529

I understand you are asking for this to download all assets before doing any installation. I’m wondering if it’s important to complete all downloads before any install happens.

Due to the way formula installer and dependency resolution works it would be much more achievable to make sure that each asset is downloaded before that asset is unlinked but in some cases dependencies may be installed before dependent packages are installed

2. > This is only used in Patch#apply. How about calling fetch before resource.unpack there?

With the former behavior, `resource#fetch` was being called inside `resource#stage` right before `#unpack` is called.  When I run tests, following the code path of patch, it will call `formula#brew` which leads to `resource#stage` and inevitably, needing to fetch before `#unpack` happens there. `Patch#apply` is not being hit here in the tests.

https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/c32d96d4d38a3be34a47cb6fc41a14a5540b813c/Library/Homebrew/resource.rb#L70-L77

issue_context.title: brew upgrade should download new version first
issue_context.body:
# A detailed description of the proposed feature

When upgrading a bottle, first download the new version, then remove the old one and, finally, install the new.

# The motivation for the feature

When upgrading things, the thing being upgraded will be unavailable for some time, since its first removed and then the download starts.

I regularly run `brew upgrade` and keep working since it takes some time... and often what I'm using (e.g. `go`) becomes unavailable during the process.

This can also lead to a "broken environment" if the user looses internet connection during the download.

# How the feature would be relevant to at least 90% of Homebrew users

Probably the more common use case is being able to use the software being upgraded while its being upgraded...

It is also how other macOS apps works: the "updater" downloads the new version while you're using the currently installed one.

So I think the relevance is in "working as most users would expect" (or maybe its just me 😂).

# What alternatives to the feature have been considered

If you keep the machine up all the time, maybe a cron job to do it at 4AM or something... not many ideas though 🤔

---

Thanks for Homebrew BTW, saved me TONS of time of the years! 🙏

Hi, @Lord-V15. #prefetch is an instance method I defined. It calls two other instance methods within it and also assigns true to a new instance variable called @prefetched. @prefetched is checked later when #install is called, and if it evaluates true, there will not be another fetch.
